Package hadur2.core.policy

Class TickBudget

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.policy.TickBudget
public final class TickBudget extends Object
The tick budget (TIME-1, TIME-2): how much work the core may do this tick, as a computation level from 0 (everything) to MAX_LEVEL. Each level sheds more:
  1. surf only the nearest wave, with the three options (no second wave, no go-to);
  2. also halve k in every KNN view the gun and the surf read, and aim without the shadow weighing (GUN-7: plain D3 aim);
  3. also stop scoring the virtual guns (their ratings hold where they were).

A skipped turn drops one level for the rest of the round (TIME-2); a tick that used more than 70% of the allowance drops one more for the next tick only (TIME-1). Both are driven by what happened, never by the clock or the round number (DIAL-2).

The core never reads a clock (RES-6, CORE-2). The adapter times each call into the core and hands the measurement in with the next tick's events as a TickTime event, which HadurCore passes to tickTook(long, long); the allowance starts as the adapter's guessed constant (3 ms, the bench machine's CPU constant, since Robocode does not tell a robot its own). TIME-3: the first skipped turn proves that guess was too high for this client, so from then on tickTook(long, long) ignores the passed-in allowance and uses the tick that caused the skip as the real one, for the rest of the battle (not just the round, so it survives newRound()). A SkippedTurn event goes to skippedTurn(long). The core then reads level() and asks the static methods what that level allows.

maxLevel() and slowTicks() are this round's degradation counters, which the core copies into the round statistics.

    • tickBegan

      public void tickBegan(long time)
      RES-14: a tick begins. The core tells the budget which tick it is before it asks whether the tick runs in duress, so the quiet stretch since the last skipped turn is measured in ticks the engine ran, skipped ones included.
      Parameters:
      time - the engine's tick, as the input carries it

    • tickTook

      public void tickTook(long usedNanos, long allowanceNanos)
      TIME-1: the previous tick took usedNanos of allowanceNanos.

      Each measurement replaces the last, so a slow tick costs a level only until the next measurement arrives, one tick later. An allowance of 0 or less means it is unknown, and an unknown allowance never sheds. Once TIME-3 has learned a real allowance from a skipped turn, allowanceNanos is ignored in favour of it.

      Parameters:
      usedNanos - how long the core took on the previous tick, in nanoseconds
      allowanceNanos - the time a tick may take, in nanoseconds, before a skip has taught the real one

    • skippedTurn

      public void skippedTurn(long skippedTime)
      TIME-2: the engine skipped a turn. The round's level drops one, down to MAX_LEVEL. TIME-3: the first time this happens, the tick that caused it becomes the learned allowance for the rest of the battle — unless that measurement is too small a share (MIN_LEARNED_SHARE) of the first guess to trust. The adapter only times its own call into the core, not whatever else the engine charged the turn for (a round-end checkpoint's write, a GC pause), so a skip can arrive right after a measured tick that had nothing to do with it; without the floor, that unrelated short measurement would become a battle-long allowance and shed far more computation than the client actually needs to. RES-14: the quiet stretch counts from the tick the engine skipped, not the tick this event is processed on, which can be later.
      Parameters:
      skippedTime - the tick the engine skipped, as the event carries it

    • duress

      public boolean duress()
      RES-9, RES-14: whether the engine has skipped DURESS_SKIPS turns this round and fewer than DURESS_QUIET_TICKS ticks have passed since the last one, so the tick runs at the duress level, below MAX_LEVEL: no samples, no tree. Another skipped turn after duress has ended starts it again, and the round's skip count is not cleared.
      Returns:
      true from the third skipped turn of a round until 300 ticks pass without another, or the round ends
